summary: Henri Seyrig was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Paris (~1919–1922). He served as head of the Institut français du Proche-Orient (~1946–1967) and taught Daniel Schlumberger.
Henri d'Ollone was a scholar in Sinology and Tibetology. He completed his military education at the École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1888–1890).

Henri de Lubac worked in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a Dr.theol. from the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1926–1929). He taught at Théologat de Fourvière (~1929–1950) and served as professor at the Catholic University of Lyon (1929–1961).

Henriette Johanna Wilhelmina Salomons was an Indologist. She studied at Leiden under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (B.A. 1901) and at Utrecht under Willem Caland (~1907–1913, Ph.D.), later serving as lecturer of Dutch at the University of Copenhagen (1928–1929).

Linguist Henrik Barić studied at Graz under Rudolf Meringer (~1906–1909) and Vienna (Ph.D. ~1909–1912). He was professor at Belgrade (1920–1954), professor at Sarajevo (~1954–1957), and director of Sarajevo's Institute of Balkan Studies (~1954–1957).

Henrik Samuel Nyberg worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed a Ph.D. at Uppsala (1908–1919), where he later served as docent (1919) and docent and professor in Semitics (1931–1956).
Henrik Zilliacus was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1926–1936), where he later held a post (~1944–1974) and taught Klaus Karttunen.
Henry Alfred Whitehead was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Trinity College, Oxford (~1873–1877), and served as principal of Bishop's College, Calcutta (~1883–1899).

Henry Baily Wade Garrick worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at the Royal College of Art. He served as Cunningham's assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1880–1890) and as artist at the Geological Survey of India (1891–1911).

Henry Beveridge was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Glasgow (~1853–1856) and Queen's University Belfast (1856). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and was president of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).
Henry Bower was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vepery Seminary. He later held the post of principal Tamil examiner at the University of Madras.

Henry Chung-hung Shiu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Shek-Wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby, completed a PhD at the University of Toronto (–2006), and holds a post at Emmanuel College, Toronto.

Henry Clarke Warren worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Harvard (~1875–1879), Johns Hopkins (1879), and Oxford, under Lanman, Palmer, Greenough, Bloomfield, and Rhys Davids. He founded the Harvard Oriental Series (1891) and the Pali Text Society.
Henry Cousens was an Indologist and archaeologist who served at the Archaeological Survey of India as assistant to Cunningham (1881) and later as superintendent of Western India (1891–1910).

Henry Creswicke Rawlinson worked in Iranian, Central Asian, history, and archaeology. Educated at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University, he held posts with the East India Company (~1827–1858), Foreign Office (~1843–1859), and Royal Asiatic Society (1862–1895).

Henry Drummond Williamson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Corpus Christi College, University of Cambridge (~1874–1889). He served as a missionary with the Church Missionary Society (1877–1893).

Henry George Briggs was an Indologist and historian. He held posts as assistant secretary at the Great Indian Peninsula Railway (1856), secretary at the Bombay Municipal Corporation (1860–1862), and worked at the Public Works Department.

Henry George Keene studied at Fort William College, Sidney Sussex College, Wadham College, and East India Company College. He was a fellow at Sidney Sussex (1817) and professor of Arabic and Persian and registrar at East India Company College (1824–1834).

Henry Green worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as professor at Deccan College (1837–1857), headmaster at English School, Surat (1841), and superintendent at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy Parsee Benevolent Institution (1852–1854).

Henry Hamilton Hadley studied at Yale, Andover Theological Seminary, and Union Theological Seminary. He held posts at Union Theological Seminary as instructor (1858) and professor of Hebrew (1862), and served as professor of Hebrew at Yale (~1861–1862).
